Lena / Jai —

Thanks again for lining up the embed + rerank cutover window next month. I wanted to pull together a short, pragmatic plan so engineering and CS are aligned before we start any backfills. High level ask: confirm (1) priority document buckets, (2) acceptable read-only window for backfill (if any), and (3) an initial smoke test schedule for rerank quality.

Attached: acme_priority_batches_v1.xlsx (proposed buckets + sizes) and a one-page smoke test checklist.

Proposed approach (short):
- Priority batches: 1) product pages (P0), 2) help center articles (P1), 3) legacy blog (P2). See spreadsheet for volume estimates.
- Backfill strategy: incremental windowed backfills by bucket to avoid cloud egress spike — target 100k docs/hr for P0, then scale. We can parallelize across 4 workers.
- Vector DB: we recommend a hybrid approach — warm new vectors into a staging namespace, run rerank evals, then flip alias. Options we can support: Pinecone-style namespace/alias, Faiss on customer infra, or hosted vectorstore. Provide tradeoffs if you prefer one.
- Rerank smoke tests: baseline eval (NDCG@10, MRR@5) on a 500-query set. Pass threshold: NDCG lift >= +6% vs current model.

Next steps: if you confirm the buckets and give us a sample queries file (500–1k queries) by Friday, Marissa and Monica will schedule a two-hour smoke test window and draft the cutover runbook.

Thanks — I'll sync with Marissa on exact worker counts after we get volumes.

— Karthik

Karthik — thanks, this is helpful. We reviewed internally and the proposed buckets look correct. A few clarifications:  

- P0 (product pages) contains ~1.2M records; our retention policy means ~300k change events per month. We can accept a rolling backfill but need search to be fully available for external traffic during business hours (9am–6pm ET); would prefer heavy write/ingest during off-peak (10pm–6am ET).
- We can provide a 800-query sample set (attached acme_sample_queries.jsonl). Those are anonymized customer search queries and internal test queries.
- Regarding vector DB: we currently use a managed namespace in our cloud provider that supports aliases. If you can stage and validate in a separate namespace before alias flip, that would be ideal.

Attachment: acme_sample_queries.jsonl (800 queries)

Can you confirm whether the 100k docs/hr target you mentioned is per-worker or aggregate? Also, we need a preliminary rollback plan in case rerank regressions exceed threshold.

— Lena Ortiz

Lena / team —

Great, thanks for the sample set and the notes on traffic windows. Quick answers and an updated proposal below.

1) Throughput and workers
- The 100k docs/hr number is aggregate per-job target; we suggested 4 workers in parallel as a conservative starting point (so ~25k docs/hr/worker). We can scale to 8 workers during off-peak if your infra supports it. We will throttle automatically to keep ingestion below your egress/CPU limits.

2) Staging namespace & alias flip
- Workflow: (A) write new vectors to staging namespace, (B) run rerank evaluation, (C) run smoke tests, (D) flip alias to staging if metrics pass, (E) monitor for 24–48h with a shadow traffic mirror for rollback safety. Alias flip is fast; rollback = re-point alias back to prior namespace and disable new namespace read.

3) Rerank evals & pass/fail criteria
- We recommend two eval phases: offline (batch NDCG@10, MRR@5 on the 800-query holdout) and live smoke (A/B sample traffic at 5% for 2 hours).
- Acceptance criteria: offline NDCG lift >= +6% and live NDCG within ±2% of offline expectations. If live NDCG drops more than 3% vs baseline or error rate increases >0.5%, trigger immediate rollback.

4) Backfill windowing approach (to minimize user impact)
- Plan: P0 windowed backfill in 12-hour slices with incremental alias checkpoint every slice. During business hours we restrict to 1 worker (lower throughput) and run catch-up off-peak. This preserves search availability while progressing the backfill.

5) Rollback stub: documented in rerank_smoke_test_checklist.md (attached). It includes play-by-play rollback commands, contact list, and monitoring dashboards.

Proposed dates: start staged backfill Monday 24 May (off-peak kickoff), run staging validation for 48 hours, plan alias flip Thursday 27 May evening PST. Can you confirm holidays or blackout dates?

— Marissa Cole
Senior Technical Program Manager, Customer Onboarding | Redwood Inference
